headline: HD Hyundai Robotics disclosed exposure of website subscriber data, and Peninsula Energy reported a cyber incident at its Wyoming uranium project. South Korea’s privacy regulator opened an investigation into the KEPCO breach, which the utility said affected 650,487 billing users.

incidents.what: The privacy regulator opened an investigation after KEPCO confirmed exposure of 650,487 billing users and separately treated all 869,761 procurement users as potentially affected.
The hospital director said encrypted databases and disrupted phones and clinical systems forced three sites to postpone non-urgent care.
The Block estimated about $2 million in attacker proceeds and separately valued later withdrawals from Fusionist’s bridge reserves at about $3.7 million.
Peninsula Energy said an incident at the Lance uranium project would temporarily affect operations and that its administrative systems were not breached.
HD Hyundai Robotics said an intruder accessed a website server holding subscriber names, usernames, passwords described as encrypted, and contact details.
The brokerage confirmed that an intrusion into its customer feedback system exposed personal information, including some account and driver’s license numbers.
Police took the network offline after detecting a potential database intrusion; phones, radio and calls for service continued normally.
incidents.scale: Network offline; no evidence of personal data access

incidents.what: INC Ransom’s claim remains unverified; the company says its own systems are secure and employee immigration records may have been taken from a law firm.
FrenchBreaches reported finding 118,130 distinct email addresses in files attributed to the nonprofit, but could not establish their origin.
Kurly reported that an additional review found exposed data for 199 current or former staff and two more shoppers.
Customer notices reported theft of card numbers, expiration dates and security codes in the November 4 breach.
Have I Been Pwned indexed 355,051 distinct email addresses from the education software provider’s September sign-on registration breach.
